stage1.impression: A calm, symmetrical, credible room. The plaster, the walnut, the laminate and the warm raking sun on the wall get close to a design-magazine interior, and the pair reads at once as two green objects at a good scale. But the light is flat: sun and shade on the wall are only about half a stop apart. The idea of sun passing through green acrylic never shows, because no green light falls anywhere in the room. The near-white rug, the brightest mass in the frame, pulls the eye to the empty foreground, and a blue stripe across it gives the render away.

blocking_9: Visible green transmitted light from at least one cabinet or horn on the back wall or floor, in frame, reading as a coloured patch at a glance
Sun-to-shade ratio on the back wall of at least 2.5 stops (lit median about 220, shade median 130 or lower), so the late sun reads as real sun
The foreground rug no brighter than the lit wall, with a real pile edge and no stripe artefact
No crushed black holes in non-product shadows (credenza toe-kick above 14 median)
Plaster relief at a real scale: fine trowel texture, not oversized orange-peel bump
Cool skylight in the shade areas against the warm sun, rather than the same warm cast everywhere

defects.what: Rug renders near-white (lum median 239, brighter than the lit wall's 220) despite tint #A89A82. It is a flat slab with a hard edge and a thin blue line running diagonally across it, a texture or reflection artefact.
Credenza toe-kick is a crushed black void (lum median 4.6, crush 15%).
Floor beside the left cabinet shows no green transmitted light (r 121 > g 101). The sun-through-cabinet idea in the brief is not visible anywhere.
The right cabinet's wall shadow is neutral grey with no tint, so the speaker reads as opaque and not as tinted acrylic in sun.
Lit wall median 220 against shaded wedge median 158: about 0.5 stop. The sun is too weak against the fill for a late-afternoon photograph, and the image looks flat and evenly lit like CG.
Plaster bump reads as oversized stucco relief at this distance. It is the most 'rendered' surface in the frame.
Glazed left wall is a cold blue-grey dead strip (lum median 77) with a flat inner reveal. The smeared tree HDRI with bright sky blotches draws the eye at the frame edge.
Half a chair cut by the frame edge. The saturated tan cushion competes with the right speaker.
Horn throat crushes to pure black (17% crush). This is product, see out_of_scope; fill could open it slightly.

changes.problem: The brief's central idea, late sun passing through both cabinets, is invisible: no green light lands anywhere in the frame.

evidence.measured: floor beside the left speaker r121 g101 b76, no green. Right speaker's wall shadow [1210,420,1340,600] r215 g197 b171, neutral. With azimuth -75 and elevation 16, the horn shadows land about 2.4 m to the right of each horn, behind the right cabinet or out of frame.

change.to: azimuth -62, elevation 14 (more from the camera side, so the left horn's transmitted light lands on the back wall above the credenza, around x -0.1 m, z 0.6-1.0 m)

changes.expected: A soft-edged pale-green patch from the left horn, and a green-edged one from the right horn near the right frame edge, on the plaster above and right of the credenza. The cabinets' side faces glow brighter.

changes.problem: Sun and shade are only about half a stop apart, so the light looks like an evenly filled render, not late sun.

evidence.measured: shaded wall median 158 against lit wall [500,60,860,240] median 220. Floor sun/shade 155/99 (profile 440-1000).

change.setting: sun irradiance; lamp north irradiance; lamp bounce irradiance; sky strength; render exposure
change.to: sun 30, north 0.45, bounce 0.2, sky 0.45, exposure -0.55 (keep lit wall at the same value)

changes.expected: Lit wall stays about 215-230. Shade falls to about 110-130, a contrast of about 1.5-2 stops in the 8-bit output, so the sun shafts read as sun.

changes.problem: The rug is the brightest mass in the frame and pulls the eye into the empty foreground, and a blue stripe across it reads as an artefact.

evidence.measured: lum median 239, r249 g238 b219, against lit wall 220. A thin blue diagonal line is visible in the crop.

change.to: tint #9C8E78, tint_mix 1.0, pile 0.025, displace 0.006, res 4k. Remove the blue stripe: check the texture for a seam or stripe channel and rotate or offset it out of frame. Move the rug back 0.3 m (position y -1.2) so its front edge is cut by the frame and no hard slab edge shows.

changes.expected: Rug reads as warm oatmeal wool about 25-40 levels below the lit wall, with visible pile and no line.

changes.problem: The shadows are as warm as the sunlit areas. A real late-afternoon room has warm sun and cool skylight in the shade, and here that split is missing.

evidence.measured: shade r166 g157 b142 (warm, b-r -24). Lit r233 g219 b194.

change.setting: sun colour; lamp north colour; render white_balance_tint

changes.expected: Shade goes to neutral or slightly cool (b about equal to r). Sun patches go clearly amber.

changes.problem: The plaster relief is oversized for a wall 5.7 m from the camera and reads as CG stucco.

evidence.measured: visible blotchy relief at 1440 px. Lit-wall p5-p95 spread 64 levels inside a uniformly lit area, mostly from bump.

changes.expected: A fine, chalky lime-plaster surface. The lit wall's internal spread drops, and type over the wall becomes cleaner.

changes.problem: The credenza's toe-kick is a pure black hole that no real room photograph would show.

change.setting: prop 2 credenza lift (plinth set-back) and a low floor bounce
change.to: lift 0.85 with the plinth set back no more than 40 mm; add a small warm area lamp (0.8 x 0.3 m, irradiance 0.15, #FFE8CC) on the floor at [0, -1.0, 0.1] aimed at [0, 0.7, 0.05]

changes.expected: The toe-kick reads as dark walnut in shadow, not void.

changes.problem: The glazed left edge is a cold dead strip with a smeared exterior, which pulls the eye off the pair.

evidence.measured: lum median 77, blue-grey reveal. HDRI blur 0.004 smears branches with bright sky blotches.

change.to: strength 1.6, blur 0.0015, rotation 40 deg (a denser, darker part of the forest behind the glass); add a linen sheer curtain, half drawn, on window 2's frame-side jamb

changes.expected: The edge reads as a real window with a soft sheer catching sun, framing the room without a bright blotch.

changes.problem: A half-cropped chair with a saturated tan cushion competes with the right speaker for attention.

evidence.measured: cushion r about 170 g 100: the most saturated non-product colour in the frame, at the edge.

change.to: position [2.35, -1.6, 0.0] (only the arm and leg in frame), colour #8A7460 mix 0.8

changes.expected: The chair becomes a quiet edge cue for scale. The right speaker regains the eye.

out_of_scope.request: The woofer cover's disc reads as a flat painted circle through the front panel (measured r70 g99 b64; delta E 12.9 against cloth #6F7F66).
out_of_scope.why: This is the speaker's cover and colour, which are fixed. Light can only help: c2's lower fill and c1's side sun should give it some cloth modelling.

out_of_scope.request: The horn throat crushes to pure black (17% of the horn region).
out_of_scope.why: It is the speaker's own geometry. Do not change it. A little frontal fill from the camera-side sun in c1 may open it.
